If you're looking for an opportunity to make an impact and help shape what's next for our iconic brands, we'd love to meet you.  Apply now.
Explore life at Fortune Brands here .
Fortune Brands is hiring a Product Manager to lead the Valve and Cartridge product line within our Moen water brand.
Every Moen faucet, shower, and bath product depends on a valve or cartridge to assembly effortlessly, seal perfectly, and provide the ideal tactile feel over years of use. This core technology serves as the foundation for our water control systems. As Product Manager , you will play a critical role in generating the growth and success of Valves and Cartridges and, consequently, Moen water products as a whole.
You will shape product strategies by aligning product offerings, channels, and pricing in ways that meet both customer and business needs. You propose strategic direction, drive the roadmap, and watch your decisions show up on shelves and in people’s homes.
This role calls for curiosity, empathy, and thoughtful analysis to understand market trends and customer experiences. You will work closely with cross-functional partners to develop meaningful strategies, communicate shared goals, and contribute to outcomes that strengthen market presence over time. This entails a strong business acumen with a technical aptitude to become a SME of the inner workings of Valves and Cartridges and the products they interface with.
The ideal candidate combines strong product management capabilities with a deep understanding of fluid-control technologies and consumer-facing products. They can translate customer insights, competitive analysis, and technical requirements into a compelling product strategy, while partnering with engineering teams to deliver innovative, reliable, and market-leading plumbing or fluid-control solutions.
POSITION LOCATION: This is a hybrid position based in our world-class Deerfield, IL campus, with flexibility to work from home on Mondays and Fridays.
What you will be doing:
Development of strategic product plans by aligning performance, pricing, and supply chain with long-term business goals to support sustainable revenue and market growth.
Partner with cross-functional teams to guide new product development and innovation initiatives through the full stage-gate process.
Build collaborative relationships with external customers by sharing insights and helping identify opportunities for category growth.
Work closely with Revenue Growth Management, Sales, Analytics, and Finance teams to better understand channel dynamics and evaluate pricing strategies.
Contribute to go-to-market approaches by sharing perspectives and helping guide product and business decisions.
Collaborate with Operations, including Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and Quality, to support product launches and monitor ongoing product performance.
Advocate for the voice of the customer by developing a deep understanding of customer needs, preferences, and market trends.
Communicate product strategies and priorities clearly and thoughtfully to a variety of stakeholders.
Support sales teams through training, participation in industry events, and ongoing engagement with partners and associations.
Partner with Brand, Channel Marketing, Digital, and Commercialization teams to co-create marketing materials and promotional strategies.
Review product-related communications to ensure clarity, consistency, and accuracy.
Provide training and guidance to internal teams and external partners on product offerings and updates.
Maintain regular, supportive communication with field sales teams, including occasional travel (approximately 15%).
Contribute to additional projects and responsibilities as needed.
Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Engineering, or related field.
3-5+ years of proven experience in product management, product development, or engineering leadership for high-volume manufactured products. (We will strongly consider engineering leaders ready to move into product management.)
Experience managing products within the plumbing, kitchen and bath, or water delivery product categories OR other valve, cartridge, and fluid control technologies, including thermostatic and pressure-balancing mechanisms.
Understanding of sealing technologies, including elastomeric and ceramic components, as well as flow performance, cavitation, acoustic/noise reduction, and durability requirements.
Experience with high-volume manufactured products in industries such as plumbing, appliance, HVAC/R, water heating, beverage dispensing, irrigation, water treatment, pool and spa, or automotive fluid control systems.
Ability to translate customer needs, competitive analysis, and engineering requirements into product strategy, roadmap priorities, and successful product launches through a stage-gate or equivalent process.
Experience partnering closely with market-facing roles (such as Sales) and partnering with technical roles (engineering) to bring a quality product portfolio to market
Strong analytical and communication skills to support collaborative decision-making.
Technical aptitude and the ability to understand the engineering, functionality, and internal mechanics imperative to the product while having the business acumen (financials) to build strong business cases, derive market insights and product trends to ensure portfolio success.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word).
Willingness and ability to travel up to 15%.
Preferred Qualifications:
MBA or advanced degree in Marketing, Business, or a related field.
Ideal candidates will have experience in plumbing developing high-volume consumer, commercial, or automotive products that incorporate fluid control systems, including thermostatic and pressure-compensating valves, cartridges, elastomeric and ceramic sealing technologies, flow regulation, noise and cavitation management, and durability/lifecycle performance.
Background in building products, home improvement, or durable goods.Experience with both B2C and B2B product environments.
Familiarity with connected product technologies or smart home categories.

The Event Manager independently owns the end-to-end planning and execution of assigned US commercial marketing events, including tradeshows, conferences, customer programs, internal meetings, company events, and in-person, hybrid, or virtual experiences.The role translates marketing objectives into executable event plans and delivers a consistent, high-quality experience for internal and external audiences.
The Event Manager coordinates cross-functional partners, associations, agencies, and suppliers; manages event budgets, schedules, logistics, communications and event technology; identifies risks early; and uses established standards and post-event results to improve execution.

title: Field Service Engineer 2 - 2nd Shift
description:
This is a newly introduced shift offering at Intuitive, designed to expand our support coverage
and provide greater flexibility for our customers and teams. The role requires up to 75%
overnight travel, both within and outside your assigned territory, depending on evolving
business needs.
Second Shift FSEs will operate Monday through Friday, with working hours generally falling
between 2:00 p.m. and 11:00 p.m. This shift supports late-day procedures, extended
troubleshooting windows, and after-hours requests, ensuring seamless service across time
zones.
Weekend Traveler FSSEs will work extended shifts, typically 10:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. on Fridays
and Mondays, and either 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. or 10:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. on Saturdays and
Sundays. This role is ideal for individuals who thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and
are eager to support the mission of providing uninterrupted patient care.
Primary Function of Position
As a Field Service Engineer 2 at Intuitive, you will be an integral part of our dedicated team,
responsible for the installation, support, troubleshooting, repair, and maintenance of all our
products within your management designated area of responsibility. Your primary focus will be
to ensure that all service agreements and warranty obligations are met and surpassed, while consistently exceeding customer expectations. This role demands
expertise in electro-mechanical systems, acquired through
specialized training, as well as exceptional customer service and
communication skills. As a Field Service Engineer 2, you will have
the opportunity to work closely with our valued customers, providing technical expertise,
resolving issues, and delivering outstanding support. Join us in our commitment to excellence
and innovation as we continue to revolutionize the industry.
Essential Job Duties
• Understand and comply with all department and company policies
• Provide management with a quarterly review and assessment of your assigned area of
responsibility
• Proficiency in accurately documenting service activities, maintaining records, and
providing comprehensive reports to stakeholders
• Complete all administrative tasks in the required time frame
• Provide technical support to end-users and other Intuitive employees
• Conduct training sessions at Intuitive facilities, training centers, and hospitals
• Perform various scheduled maintenance activities such as system inspections,
preventive maintenance, software updates, system recalls, field actions, and upgrades
• Troubleshoot, diagnose, and repair all Intuitive products and associated equipment in
accordance with procedures and within designated timeframes
• Coordinate and perform system and hardware delivery and installation
• Competent in knowledge and implementation of O.R. protocol and HIPAA standards
• Complete all administrative duties, which include, but not limited to; Spare parts
inventory, Field Activity Reports, Return Material Authorizations, Expense Reports etc.
within specified timeframes
• Maintain all Intuitive-provided items, such as issued tools, calibrated tool sets,
employee vehicles, laptops, iPads, and other company-owned assets
• Support and collaborate with Intuitive teams to facilitate company goals; eg. Assist Sales
teams with trade show support, assist Genesis teams with sterile reprocessing training,
provide hospital contacts to other Intuitive teams, etc…
• Provide feedback to HQ and take part in continuous improvement projects as required
to improve processes and identify efficiencies
• Complete all required or assigned training, including equipment training for all Intuitive
products, Intuitive Surgical University classes, and professional development courses as
directed by management
• Manage all aspects of your assigned area of responsibility, including responding to
customer needs, maintaining system install base configurations, customer contacts,
establishing a rapport with assigned customer base, and providing support for customer
training and events
Required Skills and Experience
• Demonstrated ability to work effectively as part of a team, collaborating with
colleagues, customers, and other stakeholders to achieve common goals
• Demonstrated ability to identify, analyze, and resolve technical issues efficiently,
utilizing strong problem-solving skills and critical thinking abilities
• Strong time management skills with the ability to prioritize
tasks, meet deadlines, and handle multiple assignments
simultaneously while maintaining attention to detail
• Ability to Travel up to 75% and within the travel and
expense policy as required by management to fulfill the specific needs of the role

capacity, energy, experience)

• Minimum of an Associate’s degree in related field or equivalent training/experience

description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
At Intuitive, the needs of our customers are a key driver in our approach to service innovation. Within Global Services Product Management, we build deep understanding of customer needs by working closely with them to assess strengths and opportunities. We incorporate these insights into our Global Service offerings, capabilities, and digital service solutions.
The Product Manager, Global Service Offerings will play a role in Global Services innovation by defining and executing Global Service offering strategy, pricing, portfolio alignment, market research, performance analytics, and commercialization. This role will focus on the day-to-day execution and evolution of our global service offering strategy, ensuring offerings deliver measurable value for customers while supporting company growth objectives. This role will partner across regions and functions—working with Service Operations, Sales, Marketing, Contracts, Finance, and Product—to design, launch, and optimize service offerings that align with customer needs, improve outcomes, and complement our medical device portfolio.
This is a high-visibility role and directly influences recurring revenue, customer satisfaction, and the long-term success of our service business. The Product Manager will develop solution roadmaps and continuously iterate on those roadmaps based on user feedback, emerging customer and service team needs, and business objectives.
Responsibilities for this role include both upstream and downstream activities. Upstream, the Product Manager will create proposals to enhance or develop new service capabilities, draft business cases to support those proposals, and define requirements for delivery. Downstream, they will consult on end-user training curriculum and marketing opportunities as a subject matter expert on the customer experience and program services.
The Product Manager will have an understanding of the Global Services technology, Intuitive products, and associated capabilities. This role offers a unique opportunity to contribute to goals set forth by Global Services Leadership and product business units.
Essential Job Duties
Manage the lifecycle of global service contract offerings—from design and pricing to launch, performance monitoring, and retirement.
Translate customer insights, market research, and product roadmaps into clear service offerings that align to customer outcomes and business goals.
Develop business cases to support service solution proposals that demonstrate the desirability, viability, and feasibility for the proposed solution. Use proposals to secure support and funding from relevant stakeholders and leadership.
Define value propositions that are simple, differentiated, and complementary to our medical device and digital solutions portfolio.
Manage a suite of internal and external service value tools.
Partner with Finance and Commercial teams to develop pricing and offering models based on market intelligence and economic analysis.
Monitor KPIs (renewals, upgrades, margin, adoption, value realization) and use insights to refine strategy.
Ensure offerings deliver measurable, outcomes-based value to customers and align to contract frameworks.
Collaborate with regional and global stakeholders (Sales, Pricing, Marketing, Contracts, Service Ops, Legal) to launch and scale offerings effectively.
Support Marketing’s efforts to create enablement materials (service collateral, readiness guides, tender support) and train teams to ensure successful adoption.
Support contract renewals and subscription processes to drive recurring revenue growth.
Work closely with Product Management, Engineering, and Service Delivery teams to incorporate evolving support requirements into service offerings and contracts.
Partner with Customer Success, Field Service Engineering, Technical Support, Business Systems, and Digital Services to ensure operational readiness and quality of delivery.
Act as a connector and subject matter expert across global teams, ensuring alignment on strategy, execution, and outcomes.
Establish and track key performance metrics, using dashboards and analytics to measure success and identify opportunities.
Conduct competitive and market analyses to guide evolution of service strategy.
Capture and synthesize customer feedback to inform future offerings and continuous improvement.
Develop and track goals for identified priorities. Ensure goals are aligned to business unit goals and corporate objectives.
Engage in conferences, customer visits, job shadowing, and other relevant activities to build and maintain subject matter expertise and familiarity with Global Services, customer needs, and strategic opportunities.
Perform other aligned duties as specified by Global Services Leadership
Required Skills and Experience
Minimum 5 years professional experience in product management, portfolio management, service management in healthcare, medical device, or equivalent role
Demonstrated success designing and managing global service offerings/contracts, or similar offerings, including pricing, GTM execution, and lifecycle management
Experience with subscription/recurring revenue models, contract renewals, or tender processes
Strong financial and analytical acumen, with proven track record of data-driven decisions
Strong track record of leading strategic initiatives from concept through to completion
Experience building business cases, using qualitative and quantitative data, to secure funding, resources, project/program support, and contribute to budget planning/negotiations
Excellent collaboration and influencing skills; proven ability to work effectively in a highly cross-functional, matrixed global environment.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with ability to develop and present impactful presentations on complex topics for cross-functional audiences (internal and external), director/VP-level leadership, and global stakeholders
Strong results orientation, organizational skills, and project management skills; able to prioritize and manage multiple initiatives and deadlines with attention to detail
Experience investigating and defining complex problems prior to solution development
Experience with market research, voice of customer feedback, voice of service feedback, or equivalent
Self-directed with awareness to proactively seek advice when needed
Strong knowledge of the MS Office product suite
Knowledge of medical device service operations or healthcare systems is a plus.
Experience with SFDC and tableau is a plus.
Required Education and Training
Minimum Bachelor’s degree in a related field required
Working Conditions
None
Preferred Skills and Experience
MBA preferred

description:

The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Position Summary
The Sr. Manager, Regulatory Affairs for the Digital Portfolio leads regulatory strategy and execution for software-driven products, including software as a medical device (SaMD), software in a medical device (SiMD), cloud and connected applications, data and analytics tools, and AI/ML-enabled features that support surgical care. This leader builds and manages a team of regulatory professionals and serves as the senior regulatory voice to Digital, R&D, Quality, Clinical, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Legal, and Commercial partners. The role ensures that digital innovations reach customers quickly, compliantly, and sustainably across global markets.
Key Responsibilities
Regulatory Strategy and Leadership
Develop and execute global regulatory strategies for digital products, aligned with business priorities and product roadmaps.
Determine device classification, qualification, and pathway for software functions, including whether features meet the definition of a medical device or fall under enforcement discretion.
Advise cross-functional leaders on regulatory risk, timelines, and trade-offs early in the design process.
Represent Regulatory Affairs on digital product core teams and governance forums.
Manage the regulatory assessment and ongoing oversight of the non-medical device portfolio of products, including determining non-device status, maintaining supporting rationale and documentation, and ensuring claims, labeling, and software updates do not change a product's regulatory status.
Submissions and Market Authorization
Lead preparation, review, and submission of 510(k), De Novo, and other premarket submissions.
Own regulatory strategy for software change management, including determining when changes require new submissions and leveraging Predetermined Change Control Plans (PCCPs) where appropriate.
Lead interactions with FDA including pre-submission meetings and responses to deficiency requests.
Software, AI/ML, and Cybersecurity Expertise
Apply FDA software guidance and consensus standards (e.g., IEC 62304, IEC 82304-1, IEC 62366-1, ISO 14971, IEC 81001-5-1) to digital product development and documentation.
Guide regulatory strategy for AI/ML-enabled functionality, including model transparency, validation, data management, bias assessment, lifecycle monitoring, and change control; monitor evolving requirements such as the EU AI Act.
Ensure premarket cybersecurity expectations are met (e.g., FD&C Act Section 524B, SBOM, threat modeling, vulnerability management, postmarket plans) in partnership with Product Security.
Partner with Privacy and Legal on the interplay between medical device regulation and data protection requirements (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR).
Lifecycle and Compliance
Review and approve design changes, labeling, instructions for use, and promotional/digital content for regulatory compliance.
Support postmarket activities including complaint and adverse event assessment, field actions, and regulatory reporting for software issues.
Support inspections and audits (FDA, MDSAP) and contribute to quality system procedures for software and digital development.
Maintain regulatory intelligence on digital health, SaMD, AI, and cybersecurity regulations; assess impact and drive proactive readiness.
People Leadership
Recruit, develop, coach, and retain a high-performing team; set clear goals, allocate work, and foster an inclusive, collaborative culture.
Build scalable processes, templates, and tools that improve submission quality and speed.
Manage department priorities, resourcing, and budget for the digital portfolio.
Qualifications
Required
Bachelor's degree in engineering, life sciences, computer science, or a related technical field.
8+ years of regulatory affairs experience in medical devices, including 3+ years of direct experience with software, SaMD, or digital health products.
Demonstrated success leading US premarket submissions for software-containing devices.
Working knowledge of FDA regulations (21 CFR 820 / QMSR, 21 CFR Part 11), EU MDR, and software lifecycle and cybersecurity requirements.
3+ years of experience leading or managing people or cross-functional project teams.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and regulators.
Preferred
Master's degree or advanced degree in a relevant field.
Experience with AI/ML-enabled medical devices, PCCPs, and cloud-based or connected platforms.
Experience with robotic-assisted surgery, surgical data, or enterprise-scale digital ecosystems.
Regulatory Affairs Certification (RAC) or equivalent.
Experience with global markets beyond the US and EU, and direct health authority engagement.
Core Competencies
Strategic thinking: Translates evolving regulation into practical, business-aligned strategy.
Technical fluency: Engages credibly with software engineers, data scientists, and security experts.
Influence and collaboration: Builds trust across functions and drives decisions without relying on authority.
Agility: Thrives in fast-moving, iterative development environments while maintaining compliance.
Leadership: Develops talent and holds a high bar for quality and integrity.
Working Conditions
Position is based at Sunnyvale, CA. Travel up to 20% for health authority meetings, site visits, and conferences.

description:

If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
As a Senior Software Engineer – Simulation & ML Platform , you will build software platforms supporting simulation-based data generation and machine-learning development for robotic motion AI. You will work closely with Simulation Data Scientists and ML teams responsible for simulation strategy, synthetic-data design, action-model development, sim-to-real evaluation, and machine-learning experimentation. The Senior Software Engineer will translate those research and data-science requirements into reliable, scalable, and extendible software systems.
Responsibilities
Build and maintain software infrastructure for robotic simulations & ML using NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, MuJoCo or custom simulation environments.
Architect scalable pipelines for generating synthetic and procedurally varied robotic interaction data including development of APIs, configuration systems, command-line tools, and SDKs for defining and launching simulation workloads.
Build automated integration and validation pipelines for evolving simulation platforms, physics engines, and the NVIDIA AI ecosystem, enabling rapid adoption of new releases while maintaining compatibility, reproducibility, and stability across the robotics simulation software stack.
Develop AI-assisted engineering workflows for automated code refactoring, maintainability analysis, architectural consistency, and CI/CD optimization, enabling readable, modular, and sustainable codebases while improving engineering productivity across large-scale software projects.
Create reusable abstractions for robot configurations, tasks, sensors, scene assets, domain randomization, failure injection, data capture, episode termination, and evaluation.
Build tools that allow data scientists to define experiments without modifying low-level platform code. Support headless, interactive, local, cluster, and cloud-based execution.
Develop secure, GPU-enabled containerized environments for simulation, data processing, model inference, and experimentation. Develop common interfaces for robot state, coordinate frames, actions, trajectories, control commands, sensor observations, timing, and safety status.
Build tools for importing physical robot logs into analysis and simulation environments. Enable software-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop, and controlled trajectory replay where appropriate.
Collaborate with controls, embedded, systems, and robotics engineers to manage differences between simulated and physical interfaces.
Establish standards for software development, testing, documentation, code review, release management, and operational ownership.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in computer science, software engineering, computer engineering, robotics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
5+ years of industry experience developing software for simulation, machine learning, robotics, computer vision, or autonomous-systems. Experience with high-volume image, video, time-series, or scientific data and formats such as Parquet, Zarr, or HDF5.
Strong proficiency in Python and at least one additional language such as C++, Java, or TypeScript.
Experience building data-intensive applications or data-processing pipelines. Experience designing and operating production-quality backend or platform systems. Experience with asynchronous processing, distributed workers, message queues, or event-driven architectures.
Strong understanding of API design, data modeling, concurrency, failure handling, and distributed-system fundamentals.
Experience with Docker, Linux, testing, observability, and production deployment.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, MuJoCo, Gazebo, PhysX, or another robotics simulation platform. Familiarity with USD assets and scene composition.
Experience with coordinate transforms, robot kinematics, joint states, trajectory representations, sensor synchronization, or closed-loop control.
Experience with ROS or ROS 2 and GPU-enabled applications or infrastructure.
Experience with Redis, RabbitMQ, Kafka, Ray, Celery, Kubernetes, Slurm, or cloud batch systems.
Experience building scientific, engineering, ML, or internal developer tools.
Experience with PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow, MLflow, or Weights & Biases.

Primary Function of Position
We are looking for an experienced machine controls engineer to lead the development of advanced mechatronic instrumentation for patient care applications. The ideal candidate will have a proven track record of architecting and developing control and sensing software for medical robots or diagnostic instrumentation from prototype to commercialization. A strong skillset in experimental design, empirical data collection, and data analysis/visualization is critical. Experience in low-latency machine controls, high-precision optical control, and biological sample handling applications is highly desired. This position reports on-site at offices in the San Francisco Bay Area CA.
What You'll Do
Architect, design, and implement control and sensing software for advanced mechatronic instrumentation
Work hands-on with mechatronic hardware daily in system bring-up, calibration, operation, experimentation, and debugging
Lead system optimization and debugging activity with thoughtful experimental design, execution, and data analysis/visualization
Interface with embedded systems engineers and electrical engineers to develop appropriate software interfaces to lower-level controllers and firmware
Work closely with systems engineering and mechanical engineering to architect, select, and optimize electrical control boards, motors, sensors, and other hardware components
Write clean, structured and maintainable code, document software designs for various instrument configurations, inclusive of error recovery
Write and execute unit tests ensuring excellent test coverage for software code
Use scripting languages (e.g. Python) for bringing up various hardware prototypes, for test automation, and for data analysis/visualization
Generate detailed software requirements, design specifications, and software test protocols for the company’s Quality System
Work closely with a multidisciplinary engineering team and company leadership to deliver key technical milestones
Prioritize and debug reported software issues/bugs
Required Skills and Experience
BS/MS in Computer Science or related field with 8+ years industry experience, or PhD degree with 5+ years industry experience in systems control and sensing
Strong knowledge across programming languages for real-time and pseudo-real-time control (C#, C, C++) on Linux OS
Demonstrated experience in architecting and writing motion control, sensing, and state machine code for one or more diagnostic instruments or medical robots that have reached production
Experience in low-latency machine controls for time-sensitive applications
Strong experimental design, empirical data collection, and analysis/visualization skills to support design iteration and optimization using scripting languages such as Python
Experience developing medical device software per FDA requirements including software risk analysis and cybersecurity through all phases of product development lifecycle (design, implementation, debug, verification, validation and transfer to manufacturing)
Strong analytical skills and a creative mindset
Required Education and Training
• Bachelors, Master or PhD in Computer Science or related field
Preferred Skills and Experience
• Experience controlling high-speed precision optics
• Experience with instrumentation involving biological sample processing
• Experience using OpenCV for camera sensing / computer vision applications
• Strong background in performance optimization to ensure deterministic execution of pre-defined software protocols
• Experience developing / interfacing with backend software for instrument data storage and network transmission

title: Supplier Engineering Manager
description:

As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of the Position
Manage a team of Supplier Engineers with a focus on introducing new products into production and sustaining products already in production for the Multiport business unit. The successful candidate will have the ability to lead a team, and understand and solve complex issues associated with the supplier manufacturing process, quality, and business inter-relationships. This person will develop supplier quality systems and manufacturing processes to sustain suppliers and parts effectively.
Essential Job Duties
Lead a team of supplier engineers in strategic supplier selection, evaluation, development, and improvement with the goal of establishing and maintaining a high-performing, long-term, sustainable production supply chain.
Develop and implement a robust long-term supplier strategy for the product family.
Select and evaluate suppliers that fit the supplier strategy and influence critical stakeholders to utilize and maximize the use of the Production supply base.
Ensure suppliers are compliant with the Intuitive quality management system.
Manage quality and lead the team in mitigating business risks and overcoming related challenges.
Manage supplier relationships to partner with Intuitive and the supplier effectively.
Support the team in completing the Production Part Qualification deliverables: pFMEA, Special Process Validations, FAI, and Process Capability Analysis
Support transfer of parts and suppliers throughout the product development life cycle
Manage the planning and implementation of supplier change management projects using the Supplier Change Request process (SCR).
Develop and use measurement techniques for supplier part quality, capability, cost, capacity, and delivery by creating metrics to determine if an action is required.
Identify and investigate opportunities for cost reduction and/or quality improvement by collecting opportunities and creating tactics to present opportunities, perform research, and provide data-driven plans to management.
Drive the supply base to continually improve their business and manufacturing process performance to meet Intuitive’s requirements for supplier excellence using a collection of best practices in project management, Six Sigma, Lean, SPC, and negotiation.
Review, analyze, and close non-conformances, and first article inspections by judging risk analyses and justifications, determining corrective and preventive actions at suppliers (SCAR), and looking for opportunities with suppliers to eliminate recurrence.
Led the team in solving complex process issues in the manufacture of components and assemblies.
Facilitate, influence, and work cross-functionally to improve supplier engineering processes.
Required Skills and Experience
Proven ability to lead teams to solve complex technical and process problems
Proven ability to hire highly capable staff, and grow and mentor staff
Proven ability to assess cost and capacity across supply base and develop plan to meet strategic targets
Outstanding analytical skills along with good judgment
Proficient in Six Sigma and Lean Manufacturing techniques; certification preferred
Proficient in pFMEA, process validation, route cause investigation, inspection, and test techniques
Knowledge of document management systems and ERP Systems, preferably Agile and SAP
Knowledge of 21 CFR part 820 and ISO 13485 preferred
Demonstrable knowledge of a wide range of manufacturing processes, including an understanding of key input variables for quality, cost, and capacity
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including presentations to executives

The CI Lead is a core member of the Process Area Trio (Process Owner, Maintenance Lead, and CI Lead) within the KHMS Trio Excellence Pathway. The role owns the deployment, coaching, and sustainment of KHMS continuous-improvement methodologies at the process-area level to systematically eliminate losses and drive Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) improvement. Problem Solving & Loss Elimination
Train and coach Operators, Team Leaders, and Maintenance on the KHMS Problem Solving Chapter and the escalation process.
Define 5W-1H triggers based on Performance Board downtime (e.g., three consecutive hours "red" for the same reason triggers a 5W-1H) and drive use of 5Why, troubleshooting guides, and related tools.
Continuously review and update KHMS standards, implementing countermeasures (CILs, Centerlines, etc.) to eliminate losses and monitor compliance.
5S & Visual Management
Train Operators, Team Leaders, and Maintenance in 5S; assign Process Area 5S Champions; and develop/execute a 5S implementation plan across all five categories (sort, set in order, shine, standardize, sustain).
Establish shiftly 5S evaluation checks, weekly Trio/Team Leader audits, and 5S compliance tracking within the Level 1 and Daily Performance Meeting (DPM/POWR Board).
Daily Management System (DMS) Support
Support CIL (Clean, Inspect, Lube), Centerline, Defect Handling, and Breakdown Elimination routines, including health checks, and use top-loss analysis from Operational/Daily Performance Meetings to prioritize activities.
Contribute to the Daily Performance Meeting by supporting identification of root causes of top losses and driving systemic fixes and standard updates.
Coaching & Capability Building
Provide feedback and retrain the appropriate groups (Operators, Maintenance, Team Leaders) on updated standards, building autonomous ownership of KPIs and improvements at the process-area level.
Working Relationships
Works cross-functionally with the entire plant — CI Manager, Plant Manager, Trios, Functional Managers, Plant/Line 5S Champions, Team Leaders, Operators, and Maintenance Technicians.

Working knowledge of KHMS methodologies: Problem Solving (5Why, 5W-1H), 5S, CIL, Centerline, Defect Handling, and Breakdown Elimination.
Demonstrated ability to train, coach, and drive adoption of standards at the shop-floor level.
Strong facilitation and root-cause analysis skills tied to OEE and loss-elimination outcomes.

Primary schedule is day shift; must be available and willing to work all shifts (including off-shifts and weekends as needed) to deliver training, conduct health checks, and support problem-solving across the full operation.

title: Quality Lab Technician
location: Davenport Plant (New), Iowa, United States of America
description:
Job Purpose This role supports the responsibility of performing microbiological and quality testing, collecting production and environmental samples, and accurately documenting laboratory results in support of food safety and quality programs. This position works independently on 3 rd shift and must consistently follow laboratory procedures, sampling plans, and safety requirements.
Essential Functions & Responsibilities: Perform routine microbiological testing of product, environmental, water, and production samples.
Support and execute sanitation verification testing, shelf-life studies and other microbiological testing to verify critical limits for critical processes.
Collect production and environmental samples according to established sampling plans and procedures.
Perform aseptic techniques, pipetting, serial dilutions, plating, media preparation, and result interpretation
Accurately document, review, and enter laboratory results into applicable systems.
Perform required laboratory controls, equipment checks, and calibration activities.
Identify and promptly communicate OOS results, control failures, sampling issues, equipment concerns, and other testing deviations.
Participate in proficiency testing program and internal laboratory audit process for internal factory laboratories.
Perform tasks such as managing inventory as needed.
Maintain accurate sample identification, traceability, and sample integrity.
Follow GLPs, GMPs, laboratory safety requirements, and applicable food safety procedures.
Maintain a clean, organized, and safe laboratory environment.
Communicate effectively with Quality, Productions, and laboratory personnel, including shift-to-shift hand offs.
Cross-train in laboratory functions and support team coverage as needed.
Participate in laboratory improvement projects and other assigned activities.
Other duties as assigned.
Expected Experience & Required Skills: High school diploma or GED required.
Science-related education or experience, including microbiology, biology, chemistry, food science, medical laboratory science, environmental science, or a related field.
Previous laboratory or microbiology experience preferred.
Ability to learn and accurately perform laboratory testing and sampling procedures.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to accurate documentation.
Ability to work independently and prioritize multiple tasks.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills
Ability to recognize and appropriately escalate unusual results, testing issues, or potential food safety concerns.
Ability to work safely in a microbiology laboratory that handles pathogens.
Food manufacturing, environmental monitoring, or pathogen testing a plus but not required.
Must be able to work assigned shift with prompt and regular attendance, weekends or overtime as needed.
Ability to walk, sit, stand, climb, work near moving equipment, occasionally lift up to 25lbs, operate a computer, keyboard/typing, communicate in-person and via telephone, complete paperwork responsibilities.
Work Environment & Schedule This position is considered a Manufacturing plant environment with heavy machinery and equipment. Additionally, this role requires extended hours as needed in the lab. Time for collection is on the floor in a cold environment maybe occur during extended collection periods.
This is a Monday -Thursday shift starting at 5pm.
Physical Requirements
Physical demands include but not limited to
Frequent activity or conditions sustained 1/3 to 2/3 of working hours; upright stance, keyboard or text input; sedentary – occasionally exerting 0-10 lbs. of force, limited movement from workstation for brief period of time. Cold environment for collection times.

title: Quality Supervisor
location: Jacksonville Plant, Florida, United States of America
description:
Job Purpose The Quality Supervisor is instrumental to the daily success of the facility. This leader responsibility is to lead the quality food safety initiatives on off shift while supporting Sanitation supervision. This candidate can achieve this task by evaluating daily production, updating programs and documents to improve and simplify our process, and verify all Food Safety Quality and Food Defense Programs are compliant on an ongoing daily basis throughout the year so no gaps exist. Some areas of focus consist of Kraft Heinz policies, KHMS, HACCP, FDA regulations, FSSC, religious laws, and state laws. This candidate must have a mentality every day to learn the production floor processes across the facility and all the required regulatory equipment in the facility. They will be supporting the verification for the functionality of the equipment and compliance to all hourly trained programs and initiatives. This candidate must be able to coach/teach/communicate at all levels from the hourly employees to the facility manager on site.   Essential Functions & Responsibilities Be the quality supervisor leader for the department that maintains all programs to a very high Food Safety level for compliance.
Actively engaged support in planning, defining, and directing the site auditing control program to ensure compliance to all procedures, and policies, GMP standards, Kraft Heinz requirements, and regulatory, federal and local laws.
Perform assignment in accordance with 5S, Sig Sigma and lean Manufacturing initiative.
Support the KHMS system and operational standards as outlined in the plant accountability list.
Trains, mentors, and leads off shift site Quality, Maintenance, Materials, and Production team members to ensure quality program goals are met. Strong support to site KHMS/ISO Coordinator. Monitors and maintains plant KHMS program by complying to current Kraft Heinz and International Audit (FSSC/ISO) standards. Facilitate and co-lead site cross functional quality team and participate with Kraft Heinz corporate to insure successful certifications for site.
Ensure all Specification/KPI/ KHMS/FSSC/ISO/Golden Rules plans are maintained and executed
Support all internal and external inspections/regulatory visits. Support and lead off shift audit preparation activities, accompany inspector, and complete necessary reports for communication and process owner postings.
Lead follow-ups to non-conformances found and provide responses as appropriate for all off shift risks. Review and approve minor change requests.
Monitors all weekly sanitation records for compliance and follows-up to ensure adherence to programs and established limits to ensure food safety.
Leads plant sanitation improvement projects, automation, and expansion projects.
Directs and reports on overall plant sanitation programs including PSS, RSS, PIC/PEC, expansion, and extended runs.
Directs sanitation environmental control programs like clean equipment swabs, environmental monitoring, and pathogen testing.
Coordinates and conducts full sanitation audits including equipment tear downs to ensure effectiveness of equipment cleaning procedures.
Performs assignments in accordance with established Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs), policies and procedures
Support the compliance for Hold/Release documentation and dispositioning of products.
Complete and lead validation studies for all CCPs, OPRPs and other significant controls in accordance with approved methodologies.
Maintain Quality Suite to track and trend quality checks data and create new project as needed.
Perform Net content calculation analysis for New SKU to meet the NIST requirement or for retargeting for current SKUs.
Ensures compliance to Golden Rules and other Quality principles through routine auditing, reporting and trending compliance appropriately.
Provides expertise on off shift and supporting shifts while actively participating in equipment commissioning and startup, ensuring standardization of all applicable quality and food safety procedures are followed and gaps are called out for future corrective actions.
Adhere to approved Control of change procedures, to include reviewing partial HACCP plans and issuing Agile change requests, as needed. You will be point of contact for all meetings impacting third shift.
Expected Experience & Required Skills Prefer minimum of 3+ years of experience working in a quality, production, or sanitation departments within the food industry, with at least 3 years in a leadership position in a food manufacturing facility.
Prefer strong understanding of HACCP principles, food safety regulations, quality system management system, sanitation run rules, production processes, and the KHMS framework if applicable.
Prefer strong leadership, technical, communication, delegation, and organizational skills along with keen attention to detail.
Prefer being proficient in Microsoft Office, SAP, Agile, and matrix databases.
Physical Requirements The physical demands described here are representative of those minimum expectations by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee will sit, talk, walk and hear, etc. The employee at a minimum will have to stand, reach with hands and arms, and stoop or kneel. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to ten pounds, frequently lift and/or move up to twenty pounds, and occasionally lift less than fifty pounds.

BS degree in Food Science, Food Safety, Engineering, Chemistry or related technical field OR a High School Diploma/GED and 5+ years of demonstrated success in manufacturing/ quality experience.
Demonstrated leadership capabilities in leading/influencing others
Food safety risk, identification and management, HACCP and prerequisite controls, GLP’s

Knowledge of GFSI Quality Systems such as SQF, BRC, FSSC22000 or ISO9000

2-3 years of experience in a manufacturing site managing quality and food safety management systems responsible position related to food safety or Quality and food safety management system

Implement QMP related standards into the value stream and drive to full compliance.
Manage the food safety program within the value stream including achieving compliance with any required external standards (e.g. FSC 22000, GFSI, FSMA)
Responsible for the quality agenda in the value stream (Identify key priorities related to Q&FS KPI’s and  align strategy and  resource allocation within the Value Stream, monitor and report progress against agreed objectives).

Provide leadership in the implementation of the GMP/GHP and CCP/OPRP programs within the value stream to drive compliance.
PCQI for the Value Stream.

Key interface for Q&FS related activities within the value stream.
Technical input to Value Stream related activities (new equipment installation, etc.).

Follow up consumer & customer complaints within value stream.
Q&FS lead in value stream operational meetings and providing inputs required to drive the quality agenda forward.
Communicate value stream initiatives within the R&D community.
Support MSE program which may include being an active member in one of the pillars of the program.
Support other Q&FS related programs as required, Internal/External audits, trials, food defense, Sensory program, and new associates onboarding, QCC training, etc.
Development and roll out of food safety training programs as needed to build technical and functional capability in the supply team to implement and sustain compliance to Q&FS Standards.

Factory Digital Lead
Elizabethtown, PA
Step into a role where your digital expertise directly shapes our manufacturing future.
We are looking for a dynamic Factory Digital Lead to serve as a catalyst for innovation and continuous improvement. In this role, you will be the driving force behind identifying, implementing, and supporting the next generation of factory floor digital tools and automation. Working hand-in-hand with diverse cross-functional partners, you will align technological solutions with real-world factory needs. This is your opportunity to lead high-impact workstreams that optimize our cost-to-serve, eliminate inefficiencies, and champion Mars’ journey toward becoming a leaner, more agile organization.
What are we looking for?
Minimum
Bachelor's Degree in Engineering (Electrical, Mechanical, Industrial), Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related technical discipline.
3–5+ years of experience working within a manufacturing, production, or heavy industrial environment.
Proven track record of implementing digital tools, software, or automation systems on a factory floor.
Experience managing projects within strict constraints of scope, time, budget, and cash flow.
Strong familiarity with factory-floor devices and hardware integration (handhelds, industrial tablets, sensors, edge devices).
Knowledge of standard manufacturing frameworks and compliance standards (HSE, Quality & Food Safety (QFS)).
Excellent communication skills with the ability to coach, train, and build digital capability among frontline associates.Strong stakeholder management skills with a proven ability to influence cross-functional peers without direct authority.
2+ years of experience working in a technical manufacturing environment
Prior Experience within change management
Project Management experience or leading continuous improvement initiatives
Knowledge of industrial control systems networks including factory networks, distributed control systems, IoT, control devices, and hand-held electronic devices
Strong experience with implementing and managing manufacturing and data analytics digital tools. (Such as Power BI, Power Automate, ZPI, digital forms, data lakes, SAP, etc.)
Preferred
Master's Degree or specialized certifications in Digital Transformation, Smart Manufacturing, or Project Management (PMP).
6+ years of experience in a dedicated Digital Manufacturing, Industry 4.0, or OT (Operational Technology) role.
Experience working in a multinational consumer packaged goods (CPG) or food manufacturing environment (e.g., familiar with Mars-like scale).
Deep understanding of AI technology, advanced analytics, and machine learning applied to manufacturing process optimization.
Experience utilizing digital systems to support TPM (Total Productive Maintenance) and reliability engineering.
Change management experience (Prosci or equivalent) with a track record of driving high-adoption rates for new digital workflows.
Experience acting as a key liaison between local site operations and regional/global corporate program teams.
What will be your key responsibilities?
Own the site-level Digital & Automation Masterplan, defining a long-term strategic vision and identifying transformation opportunities with clear ROI.
Identify, deploy, and maintain aligned digital tools on factory-floor hardware and edge devices to optimize daily operations.
Partner with Reliability and TPM Engineers to analyze manufacturing losses and implement targeted digital or AI-driven solutions.
Drive site-level execution of Mars' Global Digitalization Program as the primary point of contact for regional workstreams.
Upskill and coach factory teams on digital tools, building associate capability and ensuring high user adoption.
Establish clear operating standards and best practices to ensure consistent and compliant usage of digital tools.
Deliver digital and automation projects on-time, in-scope, and within budget and cash flow targets.
Knowledge of industrial control systems networks including factory networks, distributed control systems, IoT, control devices, and hand-held electronic devices.
Safeguard site compliance by leveraging digital tools to meet critical HSE, QFS, and MSE standards.
Influence and collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders to align technology with daily plant needs.
Balance site-level technical support with strategic project management and continuous personal development.

description:
Job Description:
Job: Material Handler
Segment: Mars Petcare (Greenies)
Location: North Kansas City, MO
Shift: Day Shift (6:00 AM – 6:30 PM) on a 2-2-3 Schedule
Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent
Join Our Greenies Team in North Kansas City
At Mars Petcare, we are passionate about pets. Our Greenies brand is dedicated to keeping pets healthy and happy, and we manufacture our world-renowned products right here in our highly desirable, fully climate-controlled North Kansas City facility.
Being a Mars Associate is all about opportunity. The opportunity to do the kind of challenging, interesting work that shapes the world’s best-loved brands. To work with real purpose, supported by talented, friendly people from all sorts of different backgrounds.
Whether you are an experienced warehouse professional, a skilled forklift operator looking for a stable day-shift position, or a transitioning military Veteran, Reservist, or National Guard member, we welcome your unique talents! We highly value the dedication, safety-first mindset, and structured teamwork developed in the military and look forward to helping you build a successful civilian career.
Job Summary
The Material Handler is responsible for the end-to-end logistics flow within our plant. This dual-focus role handles all incoming packaging and raw ingredients, manages safe product movement inside the site, loads outbound trailers for shipment, completes all logistics paperwork, and maintains perfect inventory control. This associate works closely with production, purchasing, receiving, shipping, and quality teams to ensure seamless plant operations in a clean, temperature-controlled environment.
Key Responsibilities
Receiving & Inbound Logistics
Receive and verify all incoming raw materials, ingredients, packaging, and components against purchase orders and shipping manifests.
Use a forklift to safely unload inbound trucks and transfer materials to their correct designated storage locations.
Conduct strict quality and food safety checks on incoming materials, including collecting product samples and verifying supplier paperwork.
Collaborate with external logistics departments and freight carriers to ensure correct and safe delivery of production materials.
Material Handling & Warehouse Operations
Safely and accurately operate material handling equipment (including forklifts) to transport inventory, raw materials, WIP (work-in-process), and finished goods throughout the facility.
Support production schedules by ensuring that the correct materials are issued and staged in production areas when needed.
Stage, build, and load outbound trailers for shipment, ensuring proper cargo weight distribution and trailer utilization.
Ensure proper labeling, sorting, FIFO (First-In, First-Out) rotation, and general organization of all materials in storage areas.
Inventory, Systems, & Documentation
Scan and track material movements using warehouse management systems to ensure perfect real-time inventory accountability.
Perform daily cycle counts, participate in precision monthly inventories, and assist with formal physical audits.
Investigate inventory discrepancies promptly and report findings to management.
Generate, review, and complete accurate shipping/receiving paperwork, logging all transactions accurately into the plant database.
Safety, Quality, & Food Safety Culture
Participate and adhere to all food safety requirements, Quality Management Processes (QMPs), and site safety programs, championing a safety-first culture.
Maintain a clean, organized, and sanitary warehouse environment in accordance with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs).
Promptly report any safety, food safety, or quality concerns to leadership.
Position Requirements
Minimum Qualifications:
Education: High school diploma, GED, or equivalent civilian/military education.
Experience: Proven experience in warehouse logistics, receiving, shipping, or material handling roles.
Equipment: Demonstrated experience operating a forklift safely in an industrial or warehouse environment.
Physical Ability: Must be in good physical condition with the ability to stand and walk for extended periods, bend, reach, climb, and safely lift up to 40 pounds manually.
Technical Literacy: Working knowledge of basic computer programs for entering data, record keeping, and maintaining inventory logs.
Core Skills: Basic math skills, a keen eye for detail, strong organizational skills, and excellent written and verbal communication abilities.
Teamwork: Demonstrated ability to work in a high-performing team environment with a willingness to learn and be coached.
Military & Veteran Technical Equivalency Guide
At Mars, we recognize that your military service has prepared you to excel in logistical operations. Your training in high-stakes material movement, precision inventory tracking, and supply chain management maps directly to this role. If you served in any of the following specialties, we highly encourage you to apply:
U.S. Army: Automated Logistical Specialist (92A), Unit Supply Specialist (92Y), Cargo Specialist (88H), Motor Transport Operator (88M), Ammunition Specialist (89B). Your experience with warehouse databases, material handling equipment (MHE), and precise property book audits is an excellent fit.
U.S. Navy: Logistics Specialist (LS), Storekeeper, Aviation Storekeeper (AK). Your experience managing inventory, shipboard supply warehouses, and processing shipping manifests maps directly to our material tracking systems.
U.S. Air Force: Materiel Management (2S0X1), Traffic Management (2T0X1), Ground Transportation (2T1X1). Your training in cargo loading, receiving inspections, strict compliance with safety procedures, and inventory precision is an exact match.
U.S. Marine Corps: Warehouse Clerk (3051), Supply Administration & Operations (3043), Logistics/Embarkation Specialist (0431), Motor Vehicle Operator (3531). Your focus on cargo staging, load planning, and material handling equipment matches our shipping and receiving operations.
U.S. Coast Guard: Storekeeper (SK), Marine Science Technician.
What We Offer (Total Rewards & Benefits)
At Mars, being an associate is more than a job—it's an opportunity to build a long-term career. We provide a competitive, industry-leading package starting on your very first day:
Compensation: Competitive base pay based on experience, shift differentials, and significant overtime (OT) potential.
Annual Bonus: Eligibility for our annual performance-based company bonus and annual merit increases.
Health & Wellness: Comprehensive Medical, Vision, and Dental insurance starting on Day One.
Retirement Planning: An exceptional 401(k) program with up to 6% company match.
Work-Life Balance: Generous paid vacation time, paid holidays, and predictable rotating 2-2-3 day shifts.
Family Support: Paid Parental Leave, plus Short-Term and Long-Term Disability.
Career Growth: Access to top-tier learning and development through Mars University.
Onsite Perks: Access to our onsite gym.
About Mars, Incorporated
Mars is a family-owned business with over a century of history making diverse products and offering services for people and the pets people love. We produce some of the world’s best-loved brands: M&M’s®, SNICKERS®, TWIX®, MILKY WAY®, DOVE®, PEDIGREE®, ROYAL CANIN®, WHISKAS®, EXTRA®, ORBIT®, 5™, SKITTLES®, BEN’S ORIGINAL®, and COCOAVIA®.
Alongside our consumer brands, we proudly take care of half of the world’s pets through our nutrition, health, and services businesses such as Banfield Pet Hospitals™, BluePearl®, Linnaeus, AniCura, VCA™, and Pet Partners™.
The Mars Five Principles – Quality, Responsibility, Mutuality, Efficiency, and Freedom – inspire our 130,000 Associates to take action every day toward creating the world we want tomorrow.

title: Circular Center Program Manager
description:
Overview
Microsoft  Cloud Operations + Innovation (CO+I) is the team behind the cloud. The Circular Center operates within the datacenter environment as a critical component of CO+I, enabling secure, compliant, and sustainable management of cloud hardware across its lifecycle. Embedded on or adjacent to datacenter campuses, Circular Centers process decommissioned servers and network equipment by securely handling data‑bearing devices (DBDs), harvesting reusable components, and routing materials for reuse or recycling to maximize value recovery. By integrating tightly with datacenter operations, supply chain systems, and sustainability programs, the Circular Center strengthens supply chain resilience, reduces waste, and advances circular economy outcomes across Microsoft’s global cloud footprint.
The  Circular Center Program Manager provides leadership, ownership, and accountability for end‑to‑end program execution across safety, compliance, sustainability, security, and value recovery objectives. This role oversees high‑volume IT asset disposition, reuse, recycling, and reverse logistics workflows within an active datacenter environment. The position requires a dvanced operational rigor, cross‑functional influence, and data‑driven decision‑making to ensure secure processing of hardware while optimizing throughput, capacity, and cost efficiency.
You will define and manage program roadmaps, milestones, dependencies, and delivery timelines aligned to campus and regional growth. You will coordinate across datacenter operations, logistics, engineering, sustainability teams, and external vendors to ensure seamless handoffs between decommissioning, transport, and Circular Center processing. Success in this role requires executive‑level communication, proactive risk mitigation, and the ability to influence without direct authority to resolve conflicts and unblock execution in a fast‑moving hyperscale environment.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. In CO+I, we operate with a growth mindset, innovate to improve sustainability and operational performance, and build a culture grounded in respect, integrity, accountability, and inclusion. The Circular Center Program Manager embodies these values by driving safe operations, trusted compliance, and measurable impact across the global cloud lifecycle.
Responsibilities
Ensures compliance with data center business units and service-level policies.
Follows and adheres to safety and security policies and procedures. Reports immediately any safety or security issues or concerns.
Own end‑to‑end program execution for Circular Center operations aligned to safety, compliance, sustainability, and value recovery goals.
Define and manage program roadmaps, milestones, dependencies, and delivery timelines.
Drive execution of high‑volume IT asset disposition, reuse, recycling, and reverse supply chain workflows.
Ensure secure handling, tracking, and destruction of data‑bearing devices (DBDs) in compliance with Microsoft security standards.
Partner with site operations to optimize throughput, capacity, and processing efficiency.
Monitor operational performance metrics and report progress, risks, and outcomes to leadership.
Identify, assess, and mitigate operational, safety, compliance, and delivery risks.

title: Data Center Technician
description:
Overview
As a Microsoft Data Center Technician (DCT), you will develop an understanding of standard processes and procedures for preparing, installing, performing diagnostics, troubleshooting, replacing, and/or decommissioning equipment under the guidance of more experienced Data Center colleagues. This opportunity will allow you to develop an understanding of our Data Center environment, familiarize yourself with security and data management procedures, and accelerate your career growth in the process. Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I DCT, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and growth opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion trainings and events, and professional certifications. Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 Data Centers in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide. With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our data center design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider. Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.  In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.   Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties
Responsibilities
Datacenter Operations
Reviews Process Change Notifications (PCNs) and develops an understanding of the impact to work execution and awareness to changes within their area of work and/or the work of others. Asks questions when they do not have required information and may provide feedback on changes to processes to experienced technicians and/or direct-line management.
Completes assigned tickets efficiently and in alignment with relevant Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) per task type with guidance from experienced technicians. Seeks guidance from more experienced technicians on challenging or complex tickets.
Receives guidance and supervision to develop an understanding of standard processes and procedures for preparing, installing, performing diagnostics, troubleshooting, replacing, and/or decommissioning IT datacenter technology(ies) and equipment. Develops and acquires a fundamental understanding of the functions of, and interactions between cabling infrastructure, network, server, and storage equipment.
Complies with Data Center business unit policies, procedures, and deadlines with guidance from experienced technicians and/or direct-line management. Escalates issues related to compliance or operational assurance activities to direct-line management.
Datacenter Work Environment Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
Contributes to a positive and effective team environment by sharing information with other shifts or technician teams, contributing in regular team meetings, asking questions, and partnering with other shifts of technician teams to complete smooth transition and effective handover of ticketed work. Encourages providing and responding to feedback received on ways to work more effectively or enhance efficiency within their team and adopts best practices shared within-and-across shifts or technician teams. Completes required security and data management training while complying with security and data management procedures/policies with guidance from other technicians. May escort third party vendors or IT support on-premises at data centers or network sites. Appropriately takes action and reports physical security access concerns and/or incidents to direct-line management or established reporting methods.
Participates in daily safety briefings. Completes required Environmental & Health Safety (EHS) training, complies with safety procedures (e.g., equipment use, lifting, electrical hazards, ladder/rolling stair use), completes required Task Hazard Analysis (THAs), and uses appropriate equipment and Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for assigned tasks. Adheres to and promotes a culture of safety, taking proactive action to alert others of safety concerns, near-misses, and/or incidents. Participates in regular cadence proactive safety observation reporting processes and systems.
Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Traveling up to 25% typically domestically to and from multiple locations during the workday, and occasionally domestically to other sites for overnight stays. May work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
Managing Service Maintains an awareness of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) through reporting dashboards, systems, for personal monthly performance discussions as needed.
Escalates and/or seeks guidance from experienced technicians or direct-line management regarding client interactions.
Develops an understanding of cross-functional Data Center processes to support partnerships with internal and external stakeholders.
Completes required training aligned to job focus areas and workloads (i.e., Break fix, Deployment, Simple Change, Decommission, IT Critical Environment) in a timely manner per direct-line management assignment(s). Observes more experienced technicians to gain hands-on experience and relevant on-the-job training (OJT). May complete additional or supplemental training to obtain or maintain relevant industry or technical certifications.
Service Delivery Develops an understanding of effective execution order strategy(ies) for assigned tasks with assistance from experienced technicians or direct-line management. Prepares, stages, sets up, and performs basic startups and shutdowns for hardware (e.g., racks, hard drives, switches) according to specific written instructions provided via checklists, guides, standard processes, emails, guidance from other technicians, and/or direction from management. May perform tasks in tandem with other technicians to comply with procedures and safety requirements.
Follows procedures to immediately communicate, report, and escalate data center technical or safety related incidents to direct-line management. May participate in bridge calls to provide details on incident status and executes on-site follow-up actions as directed if necessary.
Directly performs decommissions, simple changes (e.g., memory upgrades, OS rebuilds) and refreshes of infrastructure cabling, network, storage, and server equipment, following standard procedures whilst seeking clarification and guidance from more experienced technicians as needed. Processes data-bearing devices (DBDs) for destruction or confirms any-and-all such devices (e.g. hard-drives, solid-state drives, flash cards, etc.) contained within network, storage, or server equipment has been identified for eradication or destruction with guidance.
Performs basic diagnostics and troubleshooting with guidance from experienced technicians and/or via standard procedures to identify the cause(s) of technical issues and replace faulty components in network, storage, or server equipment with zero-to-minimal customer and/or business disruption. Develops awareness of conditions, circumstances, and scenarios which may reflect significant customer or business impact within the Data Center environment.
Learns about post-execution verification of grounding, staging, labeling, and cabling to align with all safety protocols, deployment standards, and planned Network Design Templates (NDTs). Learns about errors in deployment standards or Network Design Templates (NDTs) and escalates to relevant technicians or specialists to coordinate corrections as needed.
