title: Principal Cloud Network Engineer
description:
Overview
At Microsoft, our mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more, with Azure serving as the physical platform that underpins this mission. Azure Global Networking designs, builds and operates the optical, wide-area and edge networks that connect every Azure region to each other and to the world. This network is the lifeline of connectivity for Azure and for the services people use every day. It is also, increasingly, the infrastructure on which artificial intelligence is built. Training frontier models and serving inference at planetary scale are network problems as much as they are compute problems.
We are building the next generation of that network. That means rethinking how the optical, packet and control layers work together, moving more of the network onto open hardware and software we control, and bringing new optical and fiber technologies into production as they mature. It also means changing how the physical network itself is built and maintained, using automation and robotics to make that work faster, safer and more consistent.
As a Principal Cloud Network Engineer, you will help decide what this network becomes and then take it into production. You will own significant parts of the next generation architecture, drive the disaggregation of the hardware the network runs on, and help lead how automation and robotics change the way physical infrastructure is built and operated. This is a role for someone who wants to work across the boundaries between light, packets, software and the physical world, on a network that can never be taken offline.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Next Generation Network Design: Own significant parts of the multi-year architecture for Azure's global network across the optical, packet and control layers. Design so that capacity, topology and protection can each evolve independently, and so that no single change or failure can reach the entire backbone.
Hardware Disaggregation: Help move the network from vendor-integrated systems to open, interchangeable building blocks: merchant silicon, open network operating systems such as SONiC, open optical line systems, and pluggable and co-packaged optics. Define requirements, evaluate platforms, and work with silicon vendors, ODMs and optical suppliers to shape their roadmaps years ahead of availability.
Programmable Optical Layer: Drive how optical circuit switching, optical protection switching, coherent transport and hollow core fiber become active parts of the network design. Define the interfaces, telemetry and control models that let software see, reason about and act on the physical layer.
Physical Automation and Robotics: Find where automation and robotics can make the physical network faster, safer and more consistent to build and repair: inspection, installation quality, fiber and connector handling, hardware qualification, and repetitive lab and technician work. Run focused pilots with clear quality, safety and cost goals, and turn the ones that work into how we build.
Simulation and Safe Change: Prove designs before anything physical moves. Use and extend network simulation, digital twins and lab automation so that architectures, capacity plans and changes are validated before they reach production. Help define which physical actions can be automated, which require human approval, and which should always stay human.
AI-Driven Engineering: Apply AI and agents to our own engineering, across design, qualification, deployment and operations, so that engineers spend their time on architecture rather than on process.
Concept to Production: Take ideas from paper to lab to pilot to fleet. Write the design, build or direct the prototype, define the qualification, and stay with it through deployment at global scale.
Technical Leadership and Influence: Lead across Azure engineering, hardware, supply chain, datacenter operations, Microsoft Research and external partners without relying on reporting lines. Mentor engineers, raise the technical bar, and communicate trade-offs clearly to engineers, vendors and senior leaders.

Particular emphasis will include manufacturing engineering for GPU and AI systems using high-speed optical networking, where optical modules, high-speed cable and fiber assemblies, liquid-cooled trays, rack-level fiber infrastructure, and cross-supplier interoperability create new manufacturing, qualification, reliability, and production-ramp challenges. You will understand product and process details, identify systemic manufacturing risks, translate high-level objectives into executable plans, and deliver results by influencing cross-functional v-teams and external manufacturing partners. Manufacturing Technical Leadership : Serve as the senior manufacturing engineering lead for assigned cloud-hardware, GPU, optical-networking, and custom-silicon programs. Own the manufacturing technical strategy from early architecture through sustaining production, ensuring products can be built, tested, repaired, scaled, and supported reliably across global factories.
Design for Manufacturing and Product Industrialization : Lead DFM, DFA, testability, serviceability, packaging, automation, tolerance, and sustainability reviews with design, NPI, quality, reliability, supplier, and factory teams. Identify product and process constraints early, quantify risk, and influence architecture and design decisions to improve manufacturability, yield, cost, reliability, and time to market.

Translate product architecture into production processes, equipment and tooling strategies, assembly sequences, inspection and test methods, process controls, repair boundaries, supplier requirements, and factory qualification plans. Drive manufacturability across optical engines and modules, high-speed electrical flyover cables, multifiber connectors, fiber trunks and shuffle assemblies, accelerator trays, switch trays, rack-level fiber management, liquid cooling, and related infrastructure.
Optical Process Qualification and Factory Test: Develop and qualify contamination-controlled handling, cleaning, inspection, installation, routing, configuration-verification, and test processes for optical and high-speed interconnect assemblies. Establish factory coverage for connector integrity, cable and fiber mapping, optical-path continuity, link bring-up, telemetry, firmware interoperability, power sequencing, cooling integrity, serviceability, and system-level fault isolation.
Optical Supplier and Ramp Readiness : Drive qualification and production readiness across optical-module, laser, connector, cable, fiber-management, rack, cooling, PCB, and contract-manufacturing partners. Own supplier DFM closure, process capability, yield improvement, capacity validation, interoperability, second-source readiness, and contingency planning for maturing optical technologies.

Establish technically grounded readiness criteria for product design, process capability, equipment, tooling, fixtures, test, materials, repair, capacity, and supplier controls. Identify gaps before build start and lead cross-functional recovery actions to protect schedule, quality, capacity, and supply continuity. Provide direct technical leadership during critical factory builds and production excursions.

Assess manufacturing capability, process maturity, qualification status, compliance, capacity, interoperability, and business-continuity risks. Influence supplier investment and corrective actions while aligning sourcing, supply chain, engineering, and program stakeholders.

Develop and standardize manufacturing processes that enable repeatable production, measurable yield improvement, and scalable ramp across global manufacturing sites.
Quality Systems and Process Control : Apply statistical process control, process-capability analysis, measurement-system analysis, control plans, inspection data, and yield analytics to reduce variation and detect defects early. Drive practical automation, digital monitoring, vision inspection, AI-enabled analytics, and factory-data improvements where they provide measurable quality, efficiency, or operational value.

Establish containment, isolate root cause, verify corrective-action effectiveness, prevent recurrence, and capture reusable lessons across products, suppliers, factories, and programs.
Technical Validation and Risk Management : Own manufacturing risk identification and mitigation across NUDD, PFMEA, qualification, yield, tooling, materials, supplier readiness, schedule, and capacity. Lead engineering-change impact assessments, tolerance analyses, simulations, failure-mode evaluations, and technical trade-offs. Escalate risks with clear options, supporting data, business impact, and actionable recommendations.
Metrics, Governance, and Executive Communication : Establish dashboards and operating mechanisms for build readiness, qualification, yield, defect trends, issue aging, risk closure, supplier performance, capacity, and corrective actions. Convert detailed manufacturing data into concise technical and business narratives that enable timely decisions by engineering, program, and executive leadership.
Cross-Program Strategy and Knowledge Transfer : Identify common manufacturing challenges across product generations and develop reusable standards, roadmaps, supplier strategies, qualification methods, and process improvements. Transfer lessons learned across products, suppliers, and factories; mentor engineers; strengthen the technical capability of the broader virtual team; and create clarity and accountability in ambiguous execution environments.

title: Technical Program Manager II- Readiness Assessment & OEM Quality
description:
Overview
Microsoft's Windows Ecosystem and Commercial Engagement organization is building a closed-loop quality-readiness system for strategically important third-party OEM devices. The system connects OEM and silicon readiness, structured Readiness Assessment, controlled entrance into SelfHost, launch decisions, and post-launch learning. Its purpose is not to produce more activity or another dashboard. It is to give leaders and partners a trustworthy answer to whether a hardware-software configuration is ready to advance, what evidence supports that call, what risk remains, and who owns the next action.
As a Technical Program Manager II , you will own the program mechanisms surrounding this system: portfolio intake, partner alignment, integrated planning, readiness governance, risk and dependency management, decision records, and executive communication. You will work across Hero Device Engineering (HDE) and Hero Device Validation (HDV) program teams, OEM and silicon partners, Windows engineering, lab and test leads, data and reporting teams, SelfHost operations, and internal marketing and sales. You will turn ambiguity into an operating model and technical evidence into decisions while protecting partner trust and clear engineering accountability.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Lead the end-to-end program operating model for a portfolio of strategic OEM device readiness initiatives, from portfolio intake and scenario definition through OEM self-assessment, Microsoft Readiness Assessment, SelfHost entrance, release milestones, and post-launch learning.
Build and maintain integrated plans that connect OEM and silicon schedules, device availability, hardware and software manifests, BIOS, firmware, drivers, images, lab capacity, assessment criteria, evidence requirements, remediation work, and decision gates.
Create trusted partnerships with HDE and HDV program managers, OEM counterparts, silicon partners, engineering and quality teams, internal marketing and sales, and senior leaders. Clarify roles, service expectations, handoffs, decision rights, and escalation paths across organizational boundaries.
Drive portfolio prioritization using customer personas, product and sales importance, reviewer influence, new silicon or architecture risk, technical novelty, historical escapes, and available capacity. Make tradeoffs visible and recommend where impartial Microsoft evidence matters most.
This role requires the confidence to manage requests and weigh the resource capacity, schedule implications, and ROI. Ensuring clear outcomes, owners, capacity plan, or approved tradeoffs.
Establish and run scalable governance, including weekly portfolio reviews, milestone and readiness reviews, integrated risk and dependency tracking, gate-exception records, and decision logs. Ensure every material risk has an accountable owner, next action, date, closure evidence, and escalation path.
Facilitate readiness and entrance decisions using defined criteria, evidence confidence, hard-stop conditions, and explicit exceptions. Record the decision authority, rationale, residual risk, and evidence that would change the posture; never allow schedule pressure or incomplete data to become a silent gate bypass.
Translate assessment findings, telemetry, quality signals, and partner status into concise, decision-ready recommendations for technical and executive audiences. Separate measured facts from targets and estimates, surface unknowns and data-quality limitations, and communicate what needs to happen next.
Drive timely issue routing and follow-through across OEM, silicon, Windows, tooling, and operational owners. You will not own every technical fix, but you will make ownership gaps, aging dependencies, unresolved tradeoffs, and decisions requiring leadership action impossible to miss.
Define and improve portfolio metrics such as on-time verdicts, critical-criteria coverage, evidence completeness, receipt-to-verdict time, partner response aging, owner and disposition timeliness, capacity returned through automation, and covered post-launch escapes. Partner with data owners to preserve definitions, provenance, and confidence.
Scale the system through reusable intake contracts, templates, playbooks, service-level expectations, retrospectives, and AI-assisted workflows. Partner with lab and engineering leads on test automation and OEM self-assessment  while retaining deterministic validation, accountable human judgment, Microsoft audit authority, and OEM confidentiality.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
Bachelor's Degree AND 2+ years experience in engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development. OR equivalent experience.
1+ year(s) of experience managing cross-functional and/or cross-team projects.
Preferred Qualifications:
Bachelor's degree and 8+ years of experience in engineering, product or technical program management, product development, data analysis, or a related field, or equivalent experience; including 6+ years leading cross-functional or cross-team initiatives.
2+ years of experience managing cross-functional or cross-team projects with interdependent technical, operational, partner, and business deliverables.
Experience gathering business and technical requirements and translating them into program plans, milestones, readiness criteria, decision gates, metrics, and accountable actions.
Demonstrated experience using data to assess program health, identify and mitigate risks, manage dependencies, resolve ambiguity, and influence technical and business decisions.
Demonstrated ability to communicate complex technical and program information clearly to engineers, partner organizations, business stakeholders, and senior leaders, and to drive alignment without direct authority.
Experience with hardware-software system readiness, Windows or another operating-system platform, device development, drivers, firmware, servicing, reliability, or product-quality programs.
Experience managing external engineering relationships with OEMs, silicon vendors, suppliers, or other partners where trust, confidentiality, shared dependencies, and influence without authority are essential.
Experience designing or operating readiness assessments, launch gates, validation programs, quality reviews, risk-acceptance mechanisms, or post-launch learning loops.
Experience with Azure DevOps, Power BI, Kusto or KQL, SQL, Azure Data Explorer, or comparable planning and analytics platforms, with a solid understanding of metric definitions and data provenance.
A track record of establishing governance and reusable mechanisms that improve delivery consistency, decision quality, organizational accountability, and measurable business or customer outcomes across a highly matrixed environment.
Experience applying automation or AI to program workflows, analysis, reporting, or risk identification while preserving human accountability and sound judgment.
PMP, PgMP, Lean, Six Sigma, Agile, or comparable program-management training or demonstrated practical mastery of those disciplines.
Experience reading or writing code, queries, technical specifications, or automation logic sufficiently to collaborate effectively with software engineering, data, and tooling teams.
What Success Looks Like
Readiness verdicts and recommendations arrive before the decision gate with current configuration identity, complete evidence, clear confidence, named owners, and explicit residual risk.
Assessment turnaround improves, fewer programs are delayed by preventable intake or ownership gaps, and leaders spend less time reconciling raw data before making a decision.
OEM, silicon, engineering, lab, SelfHost, marketing, and sales stakeholders understand the operating contract and trust the process even when the evidence requires a difficult hold, remediation, or risk-acceptance decision.
Makes alignment a prerequisite for commitment and clarifies the expectation to challenge or redirect work that is not supported by agreed priorities, ownership, or capacity.
The team supports more strategic programs at fixed staffing through standardized mechanisms, automation, and responsible AI, while post-launch escapes continuously improve future assessment criteria and coverage.

description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an experienced Creative Director, Copy to join our growing in-house creative team  focused on OpenAI’s business audiences. In this role, you’ll help define how we communicate the value of OpenAI to organizations - from growing businesses and startups to global enterprises and developers building with our technology.

You’ll concept and write across integrated campaigns, product launches, customer stories, events, and other brand moments. You’ll translate complex products, technical capabilities, and business outcomes into clear, compelling ideas that resonate with decision-makers, builders, and teams adopting AI.

This is a deeply hands-on role for someone who is equally comfortable developing a big campaign platform, shaping a messaging framework, writing a film script, or refining a headline. You’ll work closely with design, production, product marketing, and communications from the earliest stages of an idea through execution.

To us, creativity is a team sport. Ideas get better when you talk them through and build on each other’s thinking. We value curiosity over certainty, kindness over ego, and the ability to balance creative ambition with clarity and decisiveness.

description:
About the Team

The Candidate Experience team ensures that every interaction candidates and interviewers have with OpenAI reflects excellence, fairness, and humanity. This team owns global coordination, interview logistics, onsite experience, Interview Programs, and the operational workflows that support all recruiting functions, from Executive and Research to Technical, GTM, and G&A. The Candidate Experience team supports a wide range of hiring modalities (from executive and research to high-volume technical roles), and we need someone who understands how to adapt across them. As OpenAI scales globally, this team plays a critical role in designing experiences that are both bespoke for highly specialized searches and scalable across rapidly growing teams and offices.

About the Role

As Global Candidate Experience Manager, you will manage CE managers and Interview Programs program managers, with global responsibility for candidate experience, coordination and interview program delivery. You will lead through the team’s managers, leads and program owners while staying close enough to daily work to understand where it breaks. You will own service quality, capacity planning, interviewer readiness, program delivery and continuous improvement across high-volume and highly bespoke hiring.

We are looking for a hands-on operating leader who can build useful AI-enabled workflows, forecast and allocate capacity, and drive complex programs from diagnosis through launch and sustained adoption. You should be comfortable reviewing a queue with coordinators, testing a workflow with technical partners, and translating a broad goal into clear owners, milestones and decisions. Your aim is to strengthen the team’s judgment and autonomy while improving candidate care.

You can move between global operating design and frontline detail, reprioritize as demand changes, and deliver high-quality work quickly despite ambiguity. You know when to standardize and automate, when a human should remain accountable, and how to explain practical tradeoffs among speed, quality, workload and fairness.

In this role, you will:

 - Manage and develop CE managers and Interview Programs program managers; support their leads and coordinators through clear priorities, delegated decisions, timely feedback and fair accountability.

 - Stay close to daily work through queue reviews, workflow walkthroughs and direct team feedback. Diagnose system, capacity and skill problems, and personally lead selected projects with clear ownership.

 - Own CE service delivery across high-volume and confidential Executive/Research hiring. Improve scheduling, routing, handoffs and onsite experience, with clear exception and escalation boundaries.

 - Build and maintain a capacity model covering demand mix, handling time, productive hours, skills, regional coverage, leave, rework and backlog recovery.

 - Set priorities across CE service and Interview Programs with recruiting leaders. Make staffing and service tradeoffs early, accounting for regional coverage, workforce continuity, interviewer bandwidth and fair coordinator workloads.

 - Drive programs and projects end to end: define the problem and success measures; manage owners, milestones, dependencies, risks, launch readiness and adoption.

 - Own Interview Programs’ operating model, priorities and delivery through accountable program owners, including readiness, onboarding, calibration support, question governance, integrity escalation and loop health. Preserve technical approval, hiring and investigation decisions with their designated owners.

 - Personally shape and test practical AI-enabled workflows with Recruiting Optimization and People Technology; use approved data, evaluation cases, human review, monitoring and rollback.

title: Mechanical Engineer, PCBA Test Infrastructure, Robotics
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a Mechanical Engineer for a senior individual-contributor role leading printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) test fixtures and infrastructure for advanced robotic systems. You will independently turn evolving requirements into working fixtures, make technical tradeoffs, and own delivery from concept and detailed design through fabrication, validation, deployment, and reliable operation.

This role combines development-lab work with deployment at contract manufacturers. You will build precision mechanical systems for board programming, functional test, and characterization, including board nests, probe plates, connector interfaces, alignment features, clamps, enclosures, and thermal interfaces. You will partner with electrical, firmware, software, manufacturing, and reliability teams to make fixtures repeatable, protective of delicate assemblies, and maintainable as board designs evolve.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 4 days a week. Travel to contract-manufacturer sites is part of the role, with timing based on build and deployment needs.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own the mechanical architecture of PCBA test stations, including frames, board nests, datum schemes, access, guarding, ergonomics, and serviceability.

 - Design probe and bed-of-nails fixtures, connector-mating mechanisms, board supports, clamps, and interchangeable tooling for programming, functional test, and characterization.

 - Use first-principles analysis and simulation to assess stiffness, probe and insertion forces, board deflection, tolerance stacks, thermal growth, and fixture life; validate key predictions on hardware.

 - Develop locating and compliance features that accommodate board and assembly variation, protect components and solder joints, and preserve contact repeatability across loading cycles and board revisions.

 - Partner with electrical engineers on test-point access, probe selection, connector engagement, ESD provisions, cable routing, cooling, and interlocks; define motion and sequencing constraints with software and controls partners.

 - Build, assemble, instrument, and debug fixtures in the lab. Establish acceptance checks for alignment, force, board strain where needed, contact repeatability, and cycle life; separate fixture problems from board failures.

 - Design safe loading, pinch-point protection, hard stops, and operator access for manual or actuated fixtures. Make wear components easy to inspect, clean, and replace.

 - Manage fabrication partners and component vendors. Release CAD, drawings, bills of materials, tolerance analyses, assembly instructions, inspection plans, and maintenance procedures.

 - Own fixture deployment and acceptance at contract manufacturers, including assembly and alignment checks, correlation with lab fixtures, operator training, and troubleshooting. Support replication, board-revision changes, and maintenance through released documentation.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have strong mechanical intuition for precision interfaces, load paths, compliance, tolerances, and the behavior of delicate electronic assemblies.

 - Move readily between analysis, CAD, vendor collaboration, and hands-on assembly and debugging.

 - Care about repeatable contact, controlled forces, operator usability, and equipment that others can maintain.

 - Take ownership from concept through reliable daily operation, adapting fixtures to evolving boards and communicating clearly across electrical, software, manufacturing, and operations teams.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Demonstrated ability to independently deliver significant precision-fixture or equipment projects from ambiguous requirements through detailed design, fabrication, validation, and sustained use.

 - Strong 3D CAD and released-drawing capability, including complete fabrication and assembly packages, bills of materials, and revision control.

 - Strong fundamentals in GD&T, tolerance analysis, locating schemes, stiffness, compliance, contact forces, and load paths.

 - Hands-on ability to work with fabrication partners, assemble and measure fixtures, diagnose failures, and iterate hardware in a lab or manufacturing environment.

 - Ability to define and execute fixture acceptance checks for alignment, force, repeatability, wear, and safe operation, using evidence to distinguish fixture problems from product variation.

 - Ability to communicate interfaces and tradeoffs across electrical, software, manufacturing, and operations teams and support deployment and troubleshooting at contract manufacturers.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - Prior PCBA test-fixture experience with board nests, probe or bed-of-nails fixtures, connector mating, and protection of delicate electronic assemblies.

 - Experience with ESD-aware tooling, thermal interfaces, actuated fixtures, interlocks, or structural and thermal simulation.

 - Experience with NX, SolidWorks, Creo, or equivalent tools; robotics hardware; or fixture replication and new-product builds at contract manufacturers.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Deliver a reusable PCBA fixture that meets agreed alignment, contact, board-support, and loading requirements, with demonstrated repeatability and protection of the assembly under test.

 - Validate fixture wear and cycle life, identify sources of intermittent contact or board loading, and improve contact-related failures, changeover time, and serviceability against agreed targets.

 - Deploy and accept the fixture at a contract manufacturer with released CAD, drawings, inspection checks, assembly instructions, spare-parts information, and maintenance procedures that enable others to reproduce and sustain it.

title: Product Reliability Engineer
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops silicon and system-level solutions designed for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. The team is responsible for building the next generation of AI-native silicon while working closely with software and research partners to co-design hardware tightly integrated with AI models. In addition to delivering production-grade silicon for OpenAI’s supercomputing infrastructure, the team also creates custom design tools and methodologies that accelerate innovation and enable hardware optimized specifically for AI.

The Compute team works on the design of our AI supercomputers, doing everything from workload modeling to influencing accelerator design. We’re leaning into our partnerships to make system and data center co-design an integral part of this process, and are looking for engineers to design AI supercomputers solutions for data center applications

This team is responsible for working with partners to optimize their hardware for our workloads, identifying promising new deep learning accelerators, and bringing those hardware platforms to production.

If you’re excited to work at the intersection of cutting edge deep learning, hardware system, and data center design this role is for you!

About the Role

We’re looking for a Product Reliability Engineer to own reliability engineering for advanced IT hardware, from printed circuit board assemblies (PCBAs) through compute and networking trays, systems, and fully integrated racks. You’ll translate operating conditions and service-life goals into reliability requirements, design and execute qualification tests, and drive failure analysis and corrective-action verification from development through production and field deployment. Working with electrical, mechanical, thermal, manufacturing, quality, and data center teams, suppliers, and manufacturing partners, you’ll use test and field evidence to improve hardware durability, serviceability, and availability.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Define reliability requirements and targets for PCBAs, trays, systems, and racks using mission profiles, expected service life, operating environments, duty cycles, and availability goals.

 - Drive design-for-reliability reviews with electrical, mechanical, and thermal engineers. Use failure modes and effects analysis (DFMEA or FMEA) and physics of failure to prioritize risks and recommend design improvements. Own component de-rating guidelines and guidance.

 - Own reliability qualification plans from new product introduction through production, defining test coverage, representative configurations, sample sizes, stress conditions, duration, pass/fail criteria, and exit evidence at each assembly level.

 - Develop and execute accelerated life and environmental tests, including temperature cycling, humidity exposure, power cycling, shock, vibration, and transport testing. Exercise hardware under representative workloads and monitor function and degradation during stress.

 - Analyze life-test and field data using Weibull and other reliability models, acceleration models, and confidence intervals. State assumptions, exposure, and uncertainty when estimating failure rates, useful life, or reliability against targets.

 - Lead failure investigations from symptom reproduction through physical root cause. Maintain failure reporting, analysis, and corrective-action records, and verify fixes through targeted testing and recurrence monitoring.

 - Review supplier reliability plans and evidence for PCBs, PCBa components/assemblies, cables, connectors, and cooling components. Identify gaps between component qualification and the stresses encountered in the integrated system or rack.

 - Work hands-on with internal and partner labs to develop fixtures, instrumentation, and test methods. Review sample traceability, test configurations, calibration, raw data, and failure capture, including on-site support at manufacturing partners.

 - Partner with manufacturing and quality engineers to establish and validate reliability screens, burn-in where justified, and ongoing reliability testing. Confirm screening detects relevant defects without consuming unacceptable product life.

 - Evaluate reliability risks introduced by assembly and integration: board strain and solder-joint damage, connector mating and retention, cable routing, fastener preload, power connections, and thermal interfaces. Partner with cooling specialists on leak integrity, material compatibility, corrosion, and cooling performance over life.

 - Plan reliability test resources, lab capacity, hardware samples, schedules, and dependencies across programs with engineering teams, technical program managers, suppliers, and manufacturing partners.

 - Present qualification results, unresolved failure modes, and residual risk at design and release reviews. Make evidence-based readiness recommendations and clearly identify test gaps, required follow-up, and decisions for accountable owners.

 - Assess reliability impact and define targeted requalification for design, component, supplier, manufacturing process, and repair changes, including firmware changes that alter hardware operating stresses.

 - Track field returns and fleet failure trends with service and data center teams. Correlate telemetry, failure analysis, and configuration history to prioritize corrective actions and feed lessons into future designs and qualification plans.

 - Validate serviceability and repeated assembly or maintenance operations, including connector mating cycles and component replacement. Work with system engineers to assess how hardware failures, redundancy, and recovery affect rack availability.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have hands-on reliability engineering experience with advanced IT hardware, such as AI/HPC servers, networking equipment, or storage systems, spanning PCBAs, electromechanical assemblies, and integrated racks.

 - Have designed, instrumented, and executed hardware reliability tests, debugged failures in the lab, and translated results into practical design or process improvements.

 - Understand failure mechanisms in electronic assemblies, including solder fatigue, PCB and laminate damage, connector wear, corrosion, and thermal or mechanical degradation.

 - Can turn mission profiles and failure risks into qualification plans, select defensible sample sizes and stress levels, and explain the assumptions and limits of accelerated testing.

 - Have led reliability qualification through development and production milestones, balancing sample availability, lab capacity, schedule, and the evidence needed for release decisions.

 - Have worked directly with component suppliers, joint design manufacturers, contract manufacturers, and external test labs to review test methods, resolve failures, and verify corrective actions.

 - Apply design for reliability, DFMEA, and physics-of-failure methods across electrical, mechanical, and thermal interfaces, and understand how manufacturing, assembly, handling, and repair affect long-term reliability.

 - Have driven structured failure analysis and corrective action using methods such as 8D, supported by electrical diagnostics, microscopy, X-ray, cross-section analysis, or specialist failure-analysis labs as appropriate.

 - Can analyze reliability and life-test data, including censored data, Weibull distributions, and confidence bounds, using tools such as Python, R, JMP, or equivalent statistical software.

 - Bring experience with high-power electronics, dense interconnects, or liquid-cooled hardware, including thermal interfaces, leak integrity, material compatibility, and serviceability.

 - Communicate technical findings and uncertainty clearly, distinguish verified root cause and corrective-action effectiveness from hypotheses, and prioritize reliability risks when requirements or designs change.

Role Summary This position is designed for emerging to mid-level Technicians who are eager to grow their technical acumen while delivering an exceptional customer experience. As part of our junior talent pipeline, you will work closely under the mentorship of senior technicians and leadership to support EV repairs, inspections, and field service operations. The ideal candidate thrives in dynamic, fast-paced environments, possesses strong communication skills, and brings a passion for innovation and adventure. While based primarily at a local service center, this role may involve remote work, traveling for mobile service, or supporting plant operations as business needs evolve. Responsibilities Vehicle Service & Repair: Perform or assist with assigned vehicle diagnosis, repairs, installations, and inspections—whether at a service center, mobile route, or remote location. Technical Guidance & Learning: Learn to identify and explain the product line, EV framework, tools, and accessories while establishing peer relationships and working under the mentorship of senior technicians. Procedure & Safety Adherence: Utilize available technical resources and follow repair procedures efficiently without compromising quality or safety. Quality Assurance: Conduct road tests on vehicles post-repair to verify repair quality and ensure operational safety. Parts & Operations Management: Assist with day-to-day parts operations, including ordering, receiving, shipping, inventory tracking, and work order/expense reporting. Documentation: Maintain proper, detailed technical notes and documentation for all completed and in-process repairs for internal and external use. Customer Interaction: Perform duties with high professionalism when interacting with customers, families, third-party affiliates, and suppliers at service facilities or outreach events. Continuous Improvement: Identify process areas for improvement, provide constructive feedback to mentorship leads, and participate in service campaigns or containment initiatives. Professional Growth: Actively engage in required training, stay current on evolving technical skills, and maintain high-quality work with minimal supervision as experience increases. Qualifications General & Operational Requirements: High School Diploma, GED, or recognized equivalency credential preferred. Minimum age of 21 years old. Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record (no suspensions or revocations within the past 3–5 years). Ability to drive a non-commercial truck and trailer is preferred. Availability for a standard 40-hour workweek, including potential shifts on weekends, holidays, early mornings, evenings, or overnights based on business needs. Flexibility for travel to regional locations or production facilities as needed. Proficient with laptops/computers in Windows or Mac environments, as well as work order management systems. Eagerness to learn, strong organizational skills, time management, and high attention to detail. Ability to perform physical tasks, including sitting, standing, walking, bending, kneeling, reaching, and lifting up to 50 lbs. Education & Experience: Graduation from an accredited automotive repair school/program is highly preferred. 0–3 years of hands-on experience in an automotive shop or technical environment; open to recent graduates looking to launch their career. Basic exposure to electric vehicle (EV) / hybrid frameworks, or experience working in fast-paced start-up environments is a plus. Technical Foundations (Junior Level Focus) Electrical & Systems: Foundational understanding of basic electricity theory (high voltage vs. low voltage awareness), basic circuit measurement tools (DVOM), and introductory exposure to reading electrical schematics. Chassis & Maintenance: Familiarity with basic hand and power tools, entry-level tire repairs, and basic vehicle alignments. Diagnostics & Workflows: Basic understanding of diagnostic workflows and troubleshooting steps under guidance. Technical Support & Remote Troubleshooting: Provide high-level diagnostic guidance to field service teams and perform remote diagnostics or repairs for issues that can be safely addressed without local vehicle access by evaluating logged vehicle data and technical schematics. Leadership & Mentorship: Coach, mentor, and train junior technicians and internal partners; foster cross-functional collaboration and lead shop-floor technical problem-solving. Advanced Tools & Methodologies: Utilize specialized diagnostic tools (e.g., PICO-Scope, PCAN, Kavaser Memorator, breakout boxes) to resolve complex electrical, high-voltage, and network faults. Quality & Process Standardization: Conduct thorough road tests to verify repair quality, champion continuous improvement processes, and drive high standards across repair workflows. Parts Operations & Systems: Oversee complex parts operations—including ordering, receiving, inventory management, and billing—to ensure quality and operational efficiency. Documentation & Technical Feedback: Produce high-quality documentation in service support and engineering systems; provide root-cause analysis and actionable feedback to field service engineers and leadership. Customer & Cross-Functional Engagement: Interact professionally with customers, suppliers, and internal teams during escalation resolutions or mobile outreach events. Qualifications General & Operational Requirements: High School Diploma, GED, or recognized equivalency credential preferred. Graduation from an accredited automotive repair school or vocational program preferred. Minimum age of 21 years old. Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record (no suspensions or revocations within the past 3–5 years). Ability to drive a non-commercial truck and trailer preferred. Availability for a standard 40-hour workweek, including weekends, holidays, early morning, evening, or overnight shifts as required. Ability to travel to regional locations or production plants as needed. Proficient in Windows/Mac environments, work order management systems, and specialized engineering/diagnostic documentation systems. Physical capability to perform occupational tasks (sitting, standing, bending, kneeling, and lifting up to 50 lbs). State mechanic certifications where required by jurisdiction (e.g., Michigan certifications in front end, suspension, steering, brakes, electrical, and HVAC). Experience & Leadership: 5 to 8+ years of automotive repair experience preferred, with extensive experience in bumper-to-bumper diagnostics. 3 to 8+ years of hands-on experience working on vehicle High Voltage (HV) systems and HV diagnostic work. Experience in leadership or supervisory roles (e.g., Shop Foreman, Team Lead, or Technical Mentor) preferred. Demonstrated background in continuous improvement, process standardization, and escalation management. Spectrum of Advanced Technical Skills: High Voltage (HV) & Power Electronics: Deep understanding of high-voltage architecture, High-Voltage Interlock Loops (HVIL), charging isolation, and safety power-down protocols using appropriate PPE. Low Voltage & Network Electronics: Advanced knowledge of automotive electronics, CAN and LIN bus network communication, reading/leveraging electrical schematics, and performing precise wiring harness repairs. Join our Team as a Career Architecture Lead!
The Career Architecture Lead Serves as S&C's subject matter expert and advisor for Career Architecture, leading the governance, maintenance, and evolution of job architecture, competencies, skills, and career pathways across the enterprise while supporting organizational effectiveness and workforce transformation initiatives across both non-hourly and production hourly (Work Elements) populations. Advises HR and business leaders on job architecture decisions, assesses gaps and inconsistencies, and conducts external research to support clear progression, leveling, and competency expectations. Develops governance practices that sustain a consistent and scalable job architecture enabling equitable and repeatable talent decisions. Ensures maintenance and evolution of S&C's competency and skills architecture to ensure alignment between workforce capabilities, career progression, talent development, and future business needs.
Key Responsibilities
Owns the continuous improvement and maintenance of job architecture and career framework standards (job families, levels, job profiles, titling alignment, competency and skills relevance, and career pathing) across non-hourly and production hourly (Work Elements) job populations.
Advises HR partners and leaders on job architecture and career framework decisions (e.g., role placement, leveling, progression alignment), applying established guidelines and governance practices to drive consistent outcomes.
Partners with Talent Management, Learning, and HR leaders to align career architecture with performance management, talent reviews, succession planning, career development, and internal mobility initiatives.
Partners with HR and operational stakeholders to ensure job architecture and career framework for production hourly roles appropriately reflects manufacturing/operational work and the shop-floor environment.
Assesses framework opportunities and gaps (e.g., leveling drift, title inflation, inconsistent profiles, irrelevant skills or competencies) and recommends updates that improve clarity, scalability, and usability.
Leads competency and skills development and refinement by aligning expectations to role profiles and levels and ensuring expectations are consistently applied across job populations.
Supports organization design initiatives by analyzing organizational structures, role alignment, spans and layers, reporting relationships, and workforce composition to improve organizational effectiveness and business performance.
Conducts external research and benchmarking related to job architecture, career frameworks, and progression practices and translates findings into practical recommendations.
Develops and maintains documentation and decision tools (e.g., role/profile guidance, titling guidance, FAQs) that enable consistent application of the architecture by HR and leaders.
Provides enablement (training, coaching, and consultative support) to improve understanding and adoption of job architecture, career framework, and governance.
Additional Functions
Supports special projects related to career frameworks, job profile quality, job catalog maintenance, and alignment of job architecture content to HR processes and systems (as applicable).
What you’ll need to succeed
Required
Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources , Business Administration, Organizational Development, Industrial/Organizational Psychology, or related field (or equivalent experience).
7+ years of progressive experience in job architecture, career frameworks, talent management, organizational effectiveness, workforce planning, or related disciplines.
Demonstrated experience implementing career frameworks and job architecture for both non-hourly roles and production hourly roles in a manufacturing/operations environment.
Working knowledge of job architecture components (job families, job levels, job profiles/descriptions, and titling conventions) and how governance drives consistency.
Experience assessing role/profile alignment, identifying gaps/inconsistencies, and recommending practical improvements.
Demonstrated experience influencing and consulting with leaders across functions and organizational levels.
Ability to build consensus across HR and business stakeholders with diverse perspectives.
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision and support/train others as needed.
Effective communication skills to explain standards clearly and influence consistent adoption.
Strong analytical and documentation skills (creating guidance, decision tools, and clear role/profile content).
Preferred
Master’s degree in a related field.
Relevant HR, talent, compensation, or job evaluation certification (e.g., SHRM, HRCI, CCP or equivalent).
Experience partnering with manufacturing/operations leaders on role clarity, progression expectations, and job structure questions for shop-floor organizations.
Experience aligning job profiles to talent processes (career development, internal mobility, learning pathways) within a Talent Management context.
Experience working with HRIS/HCM systems where job structures, profiles, or competency frameworks are maintained.

title: Senior AI Data & Analytics Engineer II
description:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role:
Want to build the data foundation powering AI and self-serve analytics at scale? As part of Samsara's Marketing Data and Analytics (MDA) Engineering team, you will shape the technical roadmap alongside our BI and Data Science peers. You will architect core Databricks pipelines, Gold Layer tables, and semantic models, turning ambitious, ambiguous business challenges into high-value data products, autonomous agents, and cross-functional automation.
This role is open to candidates residing in the US.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.
In this role, you will:
Partner on defining the strategy and multi-quarter roadmap for MDA's data and AI foundation.
Architect and own Samsara's marketing data infrastructure: ETL/ELT pipelines, Databricks Gold Layer tables, and the core data models that power segmentation, targeting, automation, and analytics.
Design the semantic layers, data dictionaries, and structured documentation that enable self-serve BI and conversational analytics, partnering with the BI team to ensure core sales and marketing KPIs are built on trusted, well-modeled data.
Translate ambiguous business questions from Marketing, Sales, and R&D into clear requirements and scalable solutions, working autonomously without dedicated PM support and influencing decisions with data and sound reasoning.
Lead complex, cross-team initiatives end to end: stand up new data pipelines and integrations quickly, manage risk across interdependent teams, and own the reliability and data quality of what ships.
Serve as the senior technical lead for the team's hardest problems: raise the bar for engineering quality and code review, remove bottlenecks that slow multiple teams, and mentor engineers and analysts.
Drive the strategic use of AI to solve ambiguous, high-impact problems: build AI-enabled data products and agents, with the integrations, retrieval pipelines, and evaluation practices that keep them reliable and trustworthy.
Identify and automate manual workflows with AI across Marketing and GTM teams, taking ideas from concept to prototype to production and influencing org roadmaps.
Ship high-quality Python and SQL, increasingly by directing agentic coding tools, while holding a high bar for reviewing and verifying AI-generated work before it reaches production.

title: technical product manager - AI
location: 1101 Church ST, Nashville, Tennessee, United States
description:
From the beginning, Starbucks set out to be a different kind of company—one that not only celebrated coffee and its rich tradition, but also built meaningful connections. We are known for developing extraordinary leaders who are guided by service to others and driven to make an impact at global scale.
We are seeking a Technical Product Manager to bridge business stakeholders and our AI engineering team — translating sourcing and procurement workflows into clear, actionable product specs that an AI team can build against. You are equally comfortable in a stakeholder review, a data schema discussion, and a sprint retro. You bring domain depth in sourcing and procurement, and enough technical fluency to be a credible partner to engineers working on LLM-powered systems.
Summary of Key Responsibilities
Functional Design & Product Documentation
Own the functional design specifications and product backlog across the AI-enabled sourcing platform — you are the author and accountable party for specs that engineering builds from directly:
Translate sourcing and procurement workflows (calendaring, market intelligence, contract management, commodity analysis) into clear, engineer-ready product requirements
Define and prioritize AI-enabled features across the platform, balancing business value, data readiness, and technical feasibility
Coordinate with business stakeholders to resolve open data, integration, and policy questions that would otherwise block engineering
Drive each module's functional spec from draft through stakeholder sign-off without losing momentum
Write clear, engineer-ready user stories and acceptance criteria across all modules; keep the sprint backlog current and prioritized
Stakeholder & Gate Management
Facilitate the structured sign-off gates that govern each module's progression from product requirements through functional design, technical design, QA, and release — no phase advances without the right approver on record
Drive AI governance checkpoints in partnership with Security, Architecture, and Legal — covering AI ethics, data privacy, model validation, and production readiness
Partner with procurement, supply chain, finance, and legal stakeholders to gather requirements, resolve open questions, and get decisions without engineering being blocked
Represent the team in leadership demos and status reviews; translate engineering delivery progress into a clear business-level narrative
Delivery & Roadmap
Own the phased delivery plan across releases: track which features are in the current MVP, which are deferred to the next release (data integration connectors, access control, document export), and which require AI enabler work before they can be built (LLM-powered features)
Coordinate data readiness with business partners — live enterprise system integration is the team's top cross-module blocker; coordinating
sample data, field mappings, and system-of-record decisions is an immediate priority
Run agile ceremonies (sprint planning, backlog grooming, demos, retrospectives); manage the cross-module sprint backlog alongside the Principal Engineer
Participate in UAT and AI output reviews — you hold the bar on whether a release is ready for stakeholders
Required Skills & Qualifications
Product Management
Proven ability to write crisp product requirements, functional design docs, and user stories with clear acceptance criteria — engineers can build directly from your specs
Experience running agile ceremonies: sprint planning, backlog grooming, retrospectives, and stakeholder demos
Skilled at prioritization under ambiguity — you can say no, explain the trade-off, and move the team forward
Ability to decompose complex workflows into phased delivery plans; familiar with MVP scoping and iterative rollout
Strong stakeholder management — comfortable facilitating reviews with both senior sponsors and individual contributors
Technical Fluency
Able to read and reason about API contracts, data schemas, and system diagrams — you don't write production code, but you can review it conceptually
Working knowledge of AI/ML product capabilities and limitations: RAG, LLM-based classification, agentic workflows — enough to scope feasibly and challenge estimates
Comfortable working in Jira, Linear, or equivalent for backlog management; familiar with Git-based doc workflows (Markdown, PR-based review)
Can interpret dashboards and basic data queries to investigate product questions without always needing engineering support
Domain — Sourcing & Procurement *(Strongly Preferred)*
Hands-on experience in or building products for Source-to-Contract (S2C) or Procure-to-Pay (P2P) workflows — e.g., RFx, supplier evaluation, contract lifecycle, commodity management, or spend analytics
Familiarity with enterprise procurement platforms (Coupa, SAP Ariba, Oracle, Jaggaer, or similar)
Understanding of sourcing calendars, commodity price benchmarking, supplier performance management, or contract analytics is a meaningful advantage
Knowledge of compliance and auditability requirements common in enterprise procurement
Communication & Collaboration
Excellent written communication — your PRDs, status updates, and decision logs are things people actually read
Experience partnering with data, finance, and legal as internal customers or reviewers
Comfortable presenting to both technical teams and non-technical business stakeholders, adjusting depth accordingly
Nice to Have
Experience as a PM or analyst at a CPG, retail, foodservice, or global supply chain organization
Prior work on AI-enabled enterprise products (not just traditional SaaS)
Familiarity with engineering delivery metrics (e.g. deployment frequency, lead time, incident rate) and how they inform product and roadmap decisions
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain, Computer Science, Engineering, or related field
3–6 years of product management or product analyst experience, with at least 1–2 years in a technically complex or AI-adjacent product environment

title: Senior Commercial Product Manager
description:
As a Commercial Operations Analyst at Zoox, you will help build and run the operational engine that drives our commercial P&L. Sitting at the center of our commercial business, you will turn pricing, promotions, and demand signals into the day-to-day and week-to-week decisions that move our growth and profitability targets—and stand up the rigor and rhythm that lets us manage those levers as we scale. This is a high-ownership role for someone who is equally comfortable in the data and in the operating cadence of a fast-moving business. You will partner closely with Product, Data Science, Fleet Operations, and Finance to translate complex commercial dynamics into clear actions, while helping establish the foundational processes that a growing Central Market Management team will be built on. It is ideal for a technical, structured operator who is energized by ambiguity and excited to shape how an autonomous mobility business is run.  In this role you will:
  • Set the objectives that pricing, promotions, and fleet deployment optimize against, from the weekly supply plan to real-time dispatch, so that decisions made in separate systems add up to one commercial plan.
  • Partner day to day with Data Science on elasticity estimation, price effects modeling, demand and supply forecasting, supply planning, and marketplace simulation, bringing a clear point of view on what to build.
  • Set the priorities for the vertical: size the expected business impact and effort of each initiative with the science and engineering leads, stack rank them, and re-rank each quarter as results come in.
  • Drive delivery across the teams that build these systems, managing dependencies, holding the schedule, and escalating early when a date is at risk.
  • Design the experiments and simulation studies that gate launches, set ship criteria and guardrail metrics before launch, make the ship call, and write the readout against the sizing that justified the work.
    Run the weekly operating cadence with Commercial Operations, Fleet Operations, and Finance: diagnose variance, propose changes to live levers, and present lever performance and roadmap status to leadership. 
    • Qualifications
  • 8+ years in product management, technical program management, or marketplace strategy roles, including significant time on marketplace products — ride-hail, delivery, travel, or similar — where pricing, incentives, matching, or supply planning was the product.
  • Demonstrated ability to specify an optimization problem in writing: given "we should price better," you can return an objective, its constraints, the data it needs, the guardrails it must respect, and the experiment that validates it.
  • A track record of driving a roadmap to completion through teams that do not report to you, changing priorities with evidence rather than authority.
  • A quantitative foundation: a degree in economics, operations research, statistics, or a similar field, and practical experience applying it — specifying or building models, running experiments, and reading their results.
  • Clear writing and presentation skills: PRDs that engineers and scientists can build from, and readouts that leadership can decide on.
  • The judgment to know which decisions need a model and which need a defensible heuristic shipped this week, in a business that is standing up its first markets.
    • Bonus Qualifications
  • Pricing or revenue management for a capacity-constrained business — airlines, hotels, freight, logistics, or energy — where the asset, not the labor pool, is the constraint.
  • Experience taking a pricing, incentives, or fleet management system from zero to production, including the operator tooling, data model, and rollback plan.
  • Deep technical grounding from graduate study in economics, operations research, statistics, or machine learning.
  • Hands-on experience with experiments where units interfere (geo and time splits, switchbacks, holdouts) and with simulation when a live test is not feasible.
